title: RRB Group D 2026 - Railway Level 1 Jobs, 10th Pass
meta_description: RRB Group D 2026 - Track Maintainer, Helper, Porter, and Level 1 posts. 10th pass eligibility, salary ₹18-25K/month, CBT + physical test.

hero.one_liner: Level 1 posts in Indian Railways - Track Maintainer, Helper, Porter, Gateman for 10th pass candidates with ITI preferred

what_is_it: RRB Group D 2026 is one of India's largest recruitment drives with 22,195 vacancies announced for Level 1 (entry-level) posts in Indian Railways. Posts include: Track Maintainer Grade-IV (largest category), Helper in various railway workshops (electrical, mechanical, signal), Porter (station operations), Pointsman (railway traffic control), Gateman (security), and other operational roles. The exam is open to 10th pass candidates (ITI is preferred but not mandatory for most positions).

The recruitment notification was released with application deadline extended to March 9, 2026. Selection process: CBT (Computer Based Test at 10th class level), Physical Efficiency Test (PET - weight lifting and running), Document Verification, and Medical examination. The CBT difficulty is low (10th class standard), making it highly accessible. The PET is the major hurdle - many candidates fail here despite clearing written exam.

Vacancies are distributed across 16 railway zones: Northern Railway (3,537 vacancies), Western Railway (3,148), Central Railway (1,979), and others. Candidates can apply to specific zones and get posting within that zone's jurisdiction. Despite 22,195 vacancies (highest among any exam), competition is intense - 1-2 crore candidates apply, making effective competition ~1 lakh per 200 vacancies (manageable with 3-4 months focused prep).

Starting salary at Level 1 is ₹18,000-21,000 basic + allowances = ₹22,500-25,380 in-hand. While lower than banking exams, railway jobs offer unmatched benefits: free rail travel (worth ₹50,000+/year), free medical (worth ₹30,000+/year), government quarters or HRA, pension, job security, and promotion to Group C (Clerk, Technician) through departmental exams.

extra_sections.heading: How RRB Group D selection works

steps.title: CBT
steps.desc: A single 100-mark computer test of 90 minutes with one-third negative marking. Your normalised score here decides who advances, so accuracy matters as much as speed.

steps.title: PET
steps.desc: Candidates up to three times the vacancies are called for the Physical Efficiency Test. It is qualifying, pass or fail.

steps.title: Document verification
steps.desc: Originals and photocopies are checked. A wrong-format certificate, especially OBC-NCL, can mean instant rejection.

steps.title: Medical exam
steps.desc: A post-specific medical, mainly vision standards, is the final gate before appointment. Some posts need A-level eyesight, so check the medical standard for the post you choose.

extra_sections.heading: Why RRB Group D is the most applied exam in India
content: RRB Group D regularly attracts 1-1.5 crore applicants for 1 lakh+ vacancies - making it the most applied government exam in India. The reason: only 10th pass is required, no age limit until 33 (general), and railway jobs come with lifetime benefits including free train travel, medical, housing, and pension.

The job roles include Track Maintainer Grade IV, Helper/Assistant in workshops, Hospital Attendant, and Gateman. Starting salary is Pay Level 1 (Rs 18,000 basic) with total monthly of Rs 28,000-35,000.
While the salary is modest, the job security, benefits, and social status of a railway employee make it highly sought after in tier 2-3 India.

extra_sections.heading: Preparation strategy for Group D CBT
content: Mathematics (25 questions): Focus on percentage, profit-loss, ratio, time-speed-distance, and simple/compound interest. Questions are 10th-level - practice RS Aggarwal arithmetic.
This section decides your score since most candidates are weak in math.

General Intelligence & Reasoning (30 questions): Coding-decoding, blood relations, direction sense, series completion, analogy, and figure counting. Practice 50 questions daily from any reasoning book.
This is the highest-scoring section if you practice regularly.
General Science (25 questions): Physics, Chemistry, Biology from Class 10 NCERT. Focus on everyday science - electricity, magnetism, acids-bases, human body systems, diseases.
Don't go deep into theory - questions test basic understanding, not detailed mechanisms.

General Awareness (20 questions): Current affairs of last 6 months, Indian history (freedom movement, ancient civilizations), geography (Indian rivers, mountains, climate), polity (Constitution basics, fundamental rights). Read a monthly current affairs magazine.

extra_sections.heading: Physical test eliminates many candidates
extra_sections.content:
PET is qualifying but eliminates 20-30% of CBT qualifiers. Male: Carry 35kg weight for 100m in 2 minutes + run 1000m in 4 min 15 sec.

Female: Carry 20kg for 100m in 2 min + run 1000m in 5 min 40 sec. Start physical training at least 3 months before expected PET date.

Daily running practice is essential.

extra_sections.heading: RRB Group D at a glance
Zone selection strategy
extra_sections.content:
Apply for the RRB zone with maximum vacancies and minimum competition. Eastern zones (RRB Kolkata, Muzaffarpur, Bhubaneswar) and Southern zones (RRB Secunderabad, Chennai) typically have more vacancies.

Northern zones (RRB Delhi, Chandigarh) have the highest competition due to population density.

items.title: Mathematics (25)
items.sub: Class 8-10 arithmetic decides your rank: number system, percentage, profit-loss, ratio, time-and-work, mensuration. Speed beats difficulty here.

items.title: Reasoning (30)
items.sub: The biggest and most scoring section: analogies, series, coding-decoding, syllogisms and Venn diagrams. Daily practice locks in easy marks.

items.title: General Science (25)
items.sub: NCERT Class 9-10 physics, chemistry and biology. Focus on basics and definitions rather than advanced theory.

items.title: GA & Current Affairs (20)
items.sub: The last six to twelve months of national current affairs plus static GK on India and the world. A monthly capsule and steady revision is enough to score well here.

extra_sections.heading: How marks are normalised and what the cutoff means
content: RRB Group D runs in many shifts over several days, and each shift gets a slightly different paper. To keep it fair, your raw score is converted into a normalised score.
Normalisation adjusts for how hard your particular shift was. Two candidates with the same raw marks can end up with different final scores depending on their shift's difficulty.
This is why a simple raw-score calculator cannot reliably tell you whether you are safe. The cutoff is set on normalised marks, not on raw marks.
To qualify you need at least 40% in the CBT as a general candidate, and 30% for SC, ST and OBC. Clearing this is only the first filter.
Final selection is by merit for the limited vacancies in your zone and category. So aim well above the bare qualifying mark, not just at it.

items.title: The work
items.sub: Track Maintainer is about 60% of posts: outdoor, physical, all-weather track work along the line. It is not a desk job, so be mentally ready for labour and shifts.

items.title: Free travel
items.sub: Free rail passes for you and your family across the Indian Railways network, a perk few other jobs offer.

items.title: Health and pension
items.sub: Treatment at railway hospitals, an NPS pension, and the security of a permanent central government job.

items.title: Promotions
items.sub: After a few years you can sit departmental exams to move up to Trackman Grade I and higher technical grades. Steady promotions and pay rises come with seniority.

extra_sections.heading: Exam day strategy
content: Arrive at the exam center 90 minutes early. Carry admit card (color printout), Aadhaar card, passport photo, and transparent water bottle.
Mobile phones are strictly prohibited - don't even carry one near the center. Wear comfortable clothes suitable for the computer-based test.
Time management: 100 questions in 90 minutes = 54 seconds per question. Attempt reasoning first (30 questions in 25 minutes) - these are the most scoring if you've practiced.
Then math (25 questions in 25 minutes). Then science (25 questions in 20 minutes).
Finally GK (20 questions in 15 minutes). Keep 5 minutes for review.
Negative marking strategy: Each correct answer = 1 mark, each wrong = -0.33 marks. You need roughly 3 correct answers to compensate for 1 wrong answer.
If you can eliminate 2 out of 4 options confidently, guessing between the remaining 2 has positive expected value. If all 4 options seem equally likely, skip the question.
For more details, see our guide on SSC GD Constable 2026. For more details, see our guide on SSC MTS 2026.

extra_sections.heading: Zone-wise vacancy analysis
content: RRB has 21 zonal offices across India. The number of vacancies varies significantly by zone, and choosing the right zone can dramatically improve your selection chances.

High-vacancy zones typically include RRB Kolkata (Eastern Railway, South Eastern Railway), RRB Secunderabad (South Central Railway), and RRB Mumbai (Central Railway, Western Railway). Low-competition zones include RRB Muzaffarpur, RRB Ranchi, RRB Bhubaneswar, and RRB Guwahati.

These zones have fewer applicants relative to vacancies because they cover less populated regions. If you have domicile or are willing to work in these areas, applying to these zones significantly increases your selection probability.

You can apply to only ONE RRB zone per notification. Choose strategically - don't default to your home zone if it's highly competitive (like RRB Delhi or RRB Allahabad which cover the most populated regions).
Research previous year cutoffs by zone before applying. The cutoff difference between zones can be 10-15 marks.

After selection, your posting is within the railways covered by your chosen RRB zone. RRB Kolkata covers Eastern Railway and South Eastern Railway - your posting will be in West Bengal, Jharkhand, or Odisha.
RRB Mumbai covers Central and Western Railway - posting in Maharashtra, Gujarat, or MP. Consider where you want to live for the next 20+ years before choosing your zone.

extra_sections.heading: Medical examination - what they check
content: The medical exam is the final stage and is strictly pass/fail - no marks or ranking. For Group D, the medical standard is CE-2 (Classification of Employment).
Vision requirement: distant vision 6/9 in better eye, 6/12 in worse eye without glasses. Color vision must be normal - color blindness is disqualifying for track-related posts.
Hearing: Must be able to hear a whispered voice at 6 meters. This is critical for track workers who need to hear approaching trains.
Blood pressure, heart condition, and respiratory fitness are checked. Hernia, hydrocele, and similar conditions may lead to temporary unfitness with option for surgery and re-examination.

If declared temporarily unfit, you get a chance to get the condition treated and appear for re-examination within a specified period (usually 3-6 months). If declared permanently unfit, there's an appeal process through Railway Medical Board.
Carry all existing medical records and prescriptions to the medical examination.

Common reasons for medical rejection: uncorrected vision problems (get your eyes checked now and consider treatment if needed), uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension (manage with medication and bring doctor's certificate), flat feet (can be waiver-eligible for non-track posts). If you know you have a medical condition, consult a railway medical practitioner before the exam.

extra_sections.heading: Previous year cutoff trends
content: RRB Group D cutoffs vary by zone, category, and year. For general category in recent cycles: RRB Kolkata 72-78 out of 100, RRB Mumbai 68-74, RRB Secunderabad 65-70, RRB Muzaffarpur 60-66.
OBC cutoffs are typically 5-8 marks lower, SC/ST 10-15 marks lower than general.
The cutoff trend has been increasing over the last 3 cycles as more candidates prepare seriously and coaching apps have made preparation accessible. Target a score of 80+ to be safe across all zones.
This means getting 60+ questions right out of 80 attempted (75% accuracy).
Section-wise ideal attempt: Reasoning 28/30, Math 18/25, Science 20/25, GK 15/20 = Total 81/100. This is achievable with 3-4 months of focused preparation.
The key is maximizing reasoning and science scores (these are practice-dependent) while doing reasonably well in math and GK.

extra_sections.heading: Books and resources
content: Mathematics: RS Aggarwal Arithmetic (best for concepts) or Kiran's SSC Mathematics (best for practice with previous year questions). Complete one book thoroughly rather than buying multiple books.
For daily practice, use Testbook or Adda247 apps - they offer free daily math quizzes targeted at RRB level.
Reasoning: RS Aggarwal Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning covers all Group D reasoning topics. MK Pandey's Analytical Reasoning is a good supplement for puzzle-based questions.
Practice from previous year RRB Group D papers - the question patterns repeat significantly across cycles.
General Science: Lucent's General Science or NCERT Class 6-10 Science textbooks. For quick revision, watch science explanation videos on Khan Academy (free) or Unacademy YouTube channels.
Science questions are conceptual - understand the 'why' behind each fact, not just the fact itself.

Current Affairs: Pratiyogita Darpan monthly magazine or any banking/SSC monthly current affairs compilation. For daily updates, follow any government exam Telegram channel that posts 10 daily current affairs points.
Don't try to read entire newspapers - curated current affairs sources are more efficient for Group D level.

items.title: Core documents
items.sub: Originals plus three photocopies of your 10th certificate and marksheet, a photo ID, and recent passport photos.

items.title: Category certificate
items.sub: OBC-NCL must be in the central government format and recently issued. State-format or expired certificates are a common reason for rejection.

items.title: SC/ST proof
items.sub: The caste certificate must come from the District Magistrate, Collector or an equivalent authority in the prescribed format.

items.title: Get it early
items.sub: Arrange a fresh central-format certificate two to three months before DV so a paperwork gap does not cost you the job.

extra_sections.heading: Application process and fees
content: Applications are filed online at rrbapply.gov.in during the notification window. You first complete a one-time registration, then apply to a single RRB of your choice.
The fee is ₹500 for general candidates and ₹250 for reserved categories, women, transgender and ex-servicemen. Part of it is refunded after you appear for the CBT.
In the form you set your post and zone preferences carefully, since these decide where you may be posted later. Think about home-state proximity before locking them.
Keep your 10th certificate, photo, signature and category certificate ready in the correct format. Aadhaar details are now used for biometric verification at the centre.
Apply early in the window. The portal slows down near the deadline, and last-minute errors are hard to fix.

extra_sections.heading: Frequently confused terms - RRB Group D vs others
content: RRB Group D is NOT the same as RRB NTPC. Group D recruits for Level 1 posts (Track Maintainer, Helper - 10th pass).
NTPC recruits for Level 2-6 posts (Station Master, Clerk - 12th/graduate). Different exams, different vacancies, different eligibility.
If you have 12th pass or graduation, appear for BOTH exams to maximize your chances of a railway job.

extra_sections.text: RRB Group D is the largest single recruitment in India - the sheer number of vacancies means that with disciplined preparation, even average students have a realistic shot at a permanent railway job.

items.title: Track Maintainer Grade-IV
items.sub: The largest category by far, maintaining tracks, alignment and sleepers and checking the line on foot. Mostly outdoor and physical work in all weather.

items.title: Pointsman / Assistant Pointsman
items.sub: Operate points and signals in yards and stations, often working in shifts.

items.title: Helper / Assistant
items.sub: Support roles in mechanical, electrical and engineering workshops and sheds.

items.title: Gateman / Porter
items.sub: Level-crossing and station support roles across several departments.

preparation_tips: Focus 60% effort on General Science (25 Qs, 25%) - it's high-scoring. Study NCERT Class 6-10 Science thoroughly: physics (motion, force, work, energy, light, electricity), chemistry (acids-bases, metals, carbon compounds), biology (human body systems, diseases, nutrition, ecosystems). Prioritize topics that repeat: force & motion, acids-bases, human anatomy.

General Awareness carries 20 marks - study: Indian geography, national projects (highways, bullet train), recent government schemes, sports news, awards, and railway-specific knowledge (zones, headquarters, recent initiatives like Vande Bharat). Read Dainik Jagran or The Hindu daily for 15 minutes.

Mathematics is 10th class level - cover: number system, BODMAS, percentage, ratio-proportion, profit-loss, simple-compound interest, average, time-work, time-distance, basic geometry, mensuration, and data interpretation. Practice 30 minutes daily using Adda247 or Testbook quizzes.
Start physical training 3 months before PET date - this is non-negotiable. Run daily and practice weight carrying with a sandbag. The exam cuts ~30-40% of candidates here; don't neglect this.

faqs.question: Is Group D salary really only ₹18K? Isn't it too low?
faqs.answer:
Starting salary is ₹18,000-21,000 basic, but add allowances (DA, HRA, night duty allowance) = ₹22,500-25,380 in-hand. For 10th pass in Tier-2/3 India, this is competitive.

Plus, railway perks (free travel worth ₹50K/year, medical, quarters) make total compensation ~₹30K/month equivalent. After 5-7 years, promotions to Group C increase salary to ₹35,000+/month.

faqs.question: I'm weak in science. Can I still clear Group D?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Science is only 25 marks (25% of 100).

If you score 15/25 in Science, 20/25 in Math, 25/30 in Reasoning, and 18/20 in GA = 78 total. With ~10 lakh candidates taking the exam and ~5 lakh securing 75+, clearing CBT is achievable without strength in Science.

However, science knowledge helps; invest 2 months to build basics.

faqs.question: What happens if I fail PET after clearing CBT?
faqs.answer:
You are eliminated. PET performance isn't scored; it's pass/fail.

Either you complete weight carry in 2 minutes and run 1000m in time, or you don't qualify further. Document Verification and Medical happen only after PET success.

Physical training is critical - don't underestimate.

faqs.question: Can females do Group D Track Maintainer work?
faqs.answer:
Yes. RRB encourages female applicants.

PET standards for females are relaxed (20 kg instead of 35 kg, 5:40 instead of 4:15). However, Track Maintainer work is outdoor, physically demanding, with shift duties (night shifts included).

Females CAN do it, but ensure you're prepared for field work and non-standard timings.

faqs.question: Zones - how to choose for posting?
faqs.answer:
During application, select your preferred RRB zone(s). Your posting will be within that zone's jurisdiction (e.g., Northern Railway covers Delhi, Punjab, Jammu-Kashmir regions).

You can apply to your home zone or any other; choice is yours. After selection, transfers between zones are possible after 5+ years of service.

faqs.question: What is the RRB Group D salary?
faqs.answer:
Every Group D post is at Pay Level 1 with a basic pay of ₹18,000. With DA, HRA, transport and other allowances, the in-hand salary works out to roughly ₹22,500 to ₹26,000 a month.

On top of pay you get free rail passes, railway medical care and an NPS pension. The exact in-hand figure depends mainly on your posting city.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in RRB Group D?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Each correct answer carries 1 mark and each wrong answer deducts 1/3 mark (0.33).

With 100 questions in 90 minutes, attempt 70-80 questions confidently rather than guessing all 100. Leaving blank is better than random guessing.

faqs.question: How many times can I attempt RRB Group D?
faqs.answer:
There's no limit on attempts as long as you meet the age criteria. General: 18-33 years, OBC: 18-36, SC/ST: 18-38.

With these age limits, you can attempt the exam 5-8 times depending on how frequently RRB conducts it (typically every 2-3 years).

faqs.question: What documents are needed for RRB Group D?
faqs.answer:
Application: Aadhaar, 10th marksheet, caste certificate (if SC/ST/OBC), PwD certificate (if applicable), passport photo, signature scan. For PET: Admit card + original photo ID.

For document verification: All original certificates - 10th marksheet, caste, domicile, medical fitness, character certificate from police station. Keep multiple photocopies of everything.

faqs.question: Can ITI holders apply for RRB Group D?
faqs.answer:
Yes. ITI holders are eligible and often get preference in workshop-related postings (Helper, Khalasi).

The minimum qualification is 10th pass - ITI is an added advantage. Some Group D posts specifically mention ITI preference for mechanical, electrical, and fitter trade workshops.

faqs.question: What is the full form of RRB Group D?
faqs.answer:
RRB stands for Railway Recruitment Board. Group D refers to the Level 1 posts in Indian Railways, such as Track Maintainer, Pointsman and Helper.

The recruitment is run through Centralised Employment Notifications, with the current one being CEN 09/2025.

changes_2026: CEN 09/2025, the active cycle, was notified in January 2026 for 22,195 Level 1 posts. Applications closed on 9 March 2026, and the CBT dates are awaited.
The earlier CEN 08/2024 cycle of 32,438 posts finished its CBT between November 2025 and January 2026. Its result is expected around May 2026, followed by the PET.
Railways now runs Group D as an annual cycle. The next notification is expected around late 2026.
Recent cycles set the age band at 18 to 36 through a one-time three-year relaxation, against the standard 18 to 33. Recheck each fresh notification.
Aadhaar-based biometric verification is now mandatory at the CBT centre.
